name: PREM-stable with GLAD-M25 lateral variations
description: PREM-stable with lateral variations in elastic structure taken from the global adjoint tomography model GLAD-M25. The G-ADOPT team chose it for Exp08 and Exp12, where the protocol leaves the elastic structure to each group.

source.citation: Lei, W. et al. (2020). Global adjoint tomography - model GLAD-M25. Geophysical Journal International 223(1), 1-21.

perturbation.relative_change: dlnvs = vs / <vs>(r) - 1 and dlnvp = vp / <vp>(r) - 1, with <.>(r) the mean of GLAD-M25 over the sphere at each depth of the dataset
perturbation.above_top_depth: the values at 6 km, the top depth of the dataset

notes: The subscript P is PREM-stable. The rule was decided by Sia Ghelichkhani on 2026-10-18. The density stays radial, so the reference state stays hydrostatic.

g-drift stores each depth of GLAD-M25 on one equal-area point set, so the plain mean of a layer is its mean over the sphere. The relative change is lateral at each depth, so the radial jumps of GLAD-M25 (650 km, and between 405 and 410 km) do not enter the moduli. PREM-stable keeps its own jumps at 400 and 670 km.
vs and vp are the Voigt averages of the g-drift dataset. GLAD-M25 is transversely isotropic in the upper mantle; the anisotropy is not used.
GLAD-M25 covers 6 to 2891 km. A g-drift query above 6 km returns the 6 km values.
GLAD-M25 is the tomography model from which the Lloyd et al. (2024) viscosity is built. Exp12 pairs the two, so its viscosity and its elastic structure come from one tomography model.
The tomography model is not in this package. A solver reads it from g-drift.
